text:
marta: noticing a big P99 latency spike on prefix-heavy routes ("/v1/generate"). p99 jumped from 120ms -> 1.8s around 03:10 UTC. prefix cache global hit-rate dropped from ~0.82 -> 0.04 in 3m.

alex: :eyes: any recent deploys or config changes?

dev-bot: deploy completed: service=runtime commit=5f3a2b9 PR=#4127 (experiment/dynamic-prefix-ttl) user=ryan env=prod ts=1778123320

kevin: grabbing kv stats now, looks like eviction storm. snippet:```
prefix_cache.hits: 1.2e2
prefix_cache.misses: 4.0e3
prefix_cache.evictions: 3.4e4
prefix_cache.items: 2.1e3
mem_used_bytes: 11.3GB
```:

ryan: uh — that deploy changed prefix TTLs for testing. diff:```- kv.prefix_ttl_seconds: 3600
+ kv.prefix_ttl_seconds: 60  # experiment, forgot to gate for prod
```

marta: that would explain the wave. TTL=60s on wide fanout prefixes + a high QPS tenant = continuous churn.

luis: pulling top tenants during the spike: acme-inc ~ 45% of prefixes, internal-loadtest ~ 12%. acme-inc traffic spiked at 03:08 (burst of small contexts). noisy tenant likely trigger.

alex: can we revert the TTL to 3600 and rewarm? also consider emergency throttle on acme-inc.

sre-oncall: plan: 1) revert config -> restart prefix cache workers 2) bump dedicated pool by +2 nodes (temp) 3) apply token-bucket throttle for tenant=acme-inc 4) monitor hit-rate and p99. executing now.

marta: ack. I'll prepare the rollback PR and include a guard to prevent TTL < 600 in prod.

ryan: PR opened and merged: runtime-config#4212 revert dynamic-ttl for prod, add validation. rolling restart prefix-cache service.

dev-bot: rollout started: service=runtime-config rollout_id=rl-778 ts=1778123440

kevin: logs while restarting showed a short surge of evictions during warmup, but after ~6 minutes the prefix_hit_rate started climbing. snapshot:```
03:16:10 prefix_hit_rate=0.06
03:19:10 prefix_hit_rate=0.24
03:22:10 prefix_hit_rate=0.61
03:25:10 prefix_hit_rate=0.78
```

luis: throttle applied to acme-inc @ 03:14 UTC (rate=120rps) — reduced noisy churn during warmup.

alex: were there any kernel-selection or batching heuristic changes in the same deploy that could have magnified memory pressure?

ryan: not in this PR. the only runtime change was the TTL experiment. separate quantization/kernel tweaks are staged but not in prod.

marta: root cause: accidental prod TTL drop combined with a noisy tenant spike -> eviction flood -> cache cold -> p99. Contributing factors: no prod guard on TTL, no early-warning on eviction rate (we only alert on mem out), and warmup is slow for high-cardinality prefixes.

kevin: mitigation done; metrics look healthy after 15m: p99 ~ 140ms, throughput normal, hit-rate ~0.8. leaving autoscale extra nodes for 30m then scale down.

ryan: follow-ups: 1) config validation (TTL>=600) 2) add eviction-rate alert (evictions/min > 5k) 3) implement transient warmup priority for prefixes with recent traffic 4) postmortem note. I'll add to the sprint.

marta: I'll draft the incident blameless postmortem and add the timeline. closing thread when postmortem is up. thanks all :heart:
